name: go_buildinfo
description: Read the build information a Go binary carries, from its bytes, and never run it. The header (`\xff Go buildinf:`, a pointer size, a flags byte) is looked for in the section that holds it (an ELF's .go.buildinfo, then its writable data segments; a PE's .data, then its writable sections; a Mach-O's __DATA,__go_buildinfo, then its __DATA segments), then by a scan of the whole file for the magic at an offset that is a multiple of 16 (a copy at another offset is counted and named, not accepted); the scan stops at max_scan_bytes (default 512 MiB) and at max_seconds, and says so. A universal binary is read slice by slice (the first 16). Both header formats are read: inline (Go 1.18 and later, two varint-prefixed strings after the header) and pointer (older: two virtual addresses of Go string headers, turned into file offsets only through a section or segment the container maps; a pointer outside them, or into the part of a segment the file does not hold, is a named problem and the module block is not guessed). The answer holds the Go version, the main package and module, every dependency (path, version, checksum, replacement) and the build settings (-compiler, -ldflags, CGO_ENABLED, GOOS, GOARCH, vcs.*) from the module block between its two 16-byte sentinels; the first `limit` rows of the dependencies and of the settings are in the answer, and each whole table is in a mode 0600 JSON Lines file named in `all_results`. `status` and `status_basis`: complete when a header was found and the module block was read from its start sentinel to its end sentinel at the declared length, every line (a header that declares no module information is complete with the version alone); `found: false` is complete only when every place that can hold a header was looked at, and says that a stripped or older binary may carry none and that absence is not 'not Go'; partial for a cut or malformed block, sentinels that are not the ones the go command writes, a line kind the tool does not read, a pointer that cannot be followed, a varint that overflows, or a limit (the module block is read to 64 MiB and 2,000,000 lines, the scan budget, the clock); unsupported for a file that is not an ELF, PE or Mach-O; failed for a file that cannot be read (a symbolic link, a pipe or a device is refused). NOT measured: whether a dependency is used or what the code does; nothing is looked up, and a checksum is the one recorded, not checked; the toolchain version and the settings are what the go command wrote, not proof of how the file was built. SENSITIVE: a build setting's -ldflags can carry a value (-X main.name=value). Every string is withheld by its shape (user-info, a secret-named key's value, token-shaped text), and the value of a build setting whose key is secret-named and of an -X flag whose symbol is secret-named is withheld whole; a secret of another shape (a plain password, a token family the rules do not name, a token split across two fields) is printed. Measured: 8,400 canaries of 17 shapes planted in 10 printed slots, none of those reached an output in that run (at most 0.8% per shape at 95%, Wilson, up to 500 per shape, for the shapes and slots of that run). That run did not bound the rate for a random base64 run of 30 characters in a `-tags` build setting, where a later independent review measured a leak: the shared rules print some random runs of 20 to 31 characters, so for such a run the bound does not hold. The canaries are random pieces, each forced to hold a lower-case letter, a capital and a digit, and the bound is for strings made so. A string of a token family drawn uniformly at random from its alphabet is not so made, and the shared rules print some of those: measured on 240 of each in marshal_inspect, which carries the same rules, and this tool prints such strings at similar rates, about 11% of sk_live_ keys, about 5% of Slack webhook URLs and about 3% of 30-character AWS secret keys reached an output; for such strings rely on those rates, not on the bound above. A checksum in the exact form `h1:` plus 43 base64 characters and `=`, and a revision of 40 or 64 hex digits in vcs.revision, are hashes the go command writes and are shown. write_values, in a job run as secret output, writes the whole text of each string the answer withheld to a mode 0600 file under $OUT; it is refused as JSON, before anything is read, outside such a job. A name, a path, a URL or a message that quotes a credential is withheld with the identifier-shaped strings, from version 4: a value given to a password, token, secret or cookie name (password=..., Pwd=..., a Cookie header), a Name/Value pair in text whose Name is a credential (a number, an array or a long Value too, and the NewValue after an OldValue), a -Password style switch, the argument of ConvertTo-SecureString, curl -u user:pass, mysql -uUSER -pSECRET, a bcrypt hash and the known token families; the text is replaced by a marker that holds only its length. Before, only identifier-shaped strings (tokens, key ids, user-info) were withheld, so these were printed. Known gaps: a pair whose Value is an array nested in another or longer than 4,096 characters, a crypt hash that is not bcrypt, and a secret that has neither a credential name nor a token shape.

path.description: A Go binary: an ELF, PE or Mach-O file, or a universal binary. A symbolic link, a pipe or a device is refused

limit.description: Rows of one table kept in the answer, 1 to 5000 (default 500: the dependencies and the build settings); the whole of a longer table is written to a file under the tool-output directory and named

max_scan_bytes.description: Bytes the scan for the header may look at in one call, 1 to 4294967296 (default 536870912); a scan that reaches it stops and the answer is partial

max_seconds.description: The tool's own time limit in seconds, from 1 to 100 (default 80); a read that reaches it stops, keeps what it read, and the answer is partial

write_values.description: Write the whole text of each string the answer withheld to a mode 0600 file under $OUT. Honoured only when the tool runs as a job (run it with secret_output: true); outside one it is refused and nothing is written
